On the left is a split DC power supply; the upper and lower DC power supplies are both labeled V_DC, and the midpoint is led out as one end of the load; on the right is the half-bridge switching leg, containing upper switch S1 and lower switch S2, and the midpoint of the bridge leg is connected to the other end of the load; the load consists of a resistor R and an inductor L in series. Reasoning: The problem gives R = 40 Ω, L = 0.3/pi H, fundamental frequency f = 50 Hz, modulation index M = 0.6, and fundamental active power P = 1.44 kW = 1440 W. The fundamental inductive reactance is X_L = 2*pi*f*L = 2*pi*50*(0.3/pi) = 30 Ω. Therefore |Z|^2 = R^2 + X_L^2 = 40^2 + 30^2 = 2500. The fundamental active power of the RL load is P = V_1,rms^2 * R / |Z|^2, so V_1,rms = sqrt(P*|Z|^2/R) = sqrt(1440*2500/40) = 300 V. The fundamental peak value is V_1,peak = 300√2 V. For this half-bridge SPWM in the figure where each DC source half is V_DC, the output fundamental peak value satisfies V_1,peak = M*V_DC. Therefore V_DC = V_1,peak/M = (300√2)/0.6 = 500√2 V.
